svg.title: Payment Platform Target Architecture
svg.text: Two deployables per server · one queue · one poster · shared Redis, Oracle and Kafka
Application servers — identical deployment on each
Shared infrastructure — one of each, not per server
FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED — workers claim
disjoint rows. No lock service needed.
Vendor direct posting writes to the queue,
never calls LMS. One poster, ever.
Zero rows = already done, ack anyway.
Unique reference sent as LMS client ref.
Needs LMS-side idempotency to fully close.
Sources 1, 2 and 4 occur on one server too.
Same controls apply to any topology.
Vendor never waits on the LMS. The challan
confirms receipt, not that the loan is updated.
Why two deployables, not five services
Split by workload profile, not domain. At ~10 journeys/sec,
independent scaling buys nothing and costs a transaction
boundary. Batch work must not share a thread pool with
verify-otp. Every duplicate risk lives in the worker, so it
gets one home. Posting can be paused without touching login.
Workers have no ingress. Only the worker posts to LMS.
A property of the drain rate, not a filter. Sustained rate
≈ batch size ÷ cycle interval. Across N servers either
divide the target N ways, or share a Redis token bucket
if the LMS enforces a hard ceiling.
Backoff on rejection — retrying at full speed into a
rate limit turns a throttle into an outage.
Open questions that change this design
1 · Is LMS posting idempotent on a client reference?
2 · Hard rate ceiling, or a request to be gentle?
3 · Partner agreement fetch — scoped or unscoped?
4 · Partner notifies, or initiates money movement?
5 · LMS concurrency ceiling → bulkhead + server count
Question 1 decides how much of the red panel you need.
